title: The businessowners policy
summary: BOP eligibility, Section I property and its valuation math, built-in business income, Section II liability limits, Michigan cancellation, and key endorsements.
objectives: Recognize which businesses are and aren't eligible for a BOP
Apply the BOP's 80% replacement cost rule instead of coinsurance
Recall BOP business income, liability aggregates and cancellation notice
Match the Protective Safeguards, Utility Services and auto endorsements

scenes.title: The businessowners policy
scenes.subtitle: Property, liability and conditions in one form for smaller businesses

beats.text: Businessowners questions are 6% of your exam, about 9 items.
beats.say: Businessowners questions are six percent of your exam, about nine items.

beats.text: We'll use the 2013 form. Revised forms apply in Michigan to policies written on or after July 1, 2025, so newer policies may differ.
beats.say: We'll use the twenty thirteen form. Revised forms apply in Michigan to policies written on or after July first, twenty twenty-five, so newer policies may differ.

scenes.title: What a BOP is, and who can buy one
scenes.src: IRMI white paper 'Businessowners Policy Basics'; ISO BP 00 03 07 13; ISO BOP Program overview (Feb. 11, 2025), pp. 2-3

items.label: Property and liability in one form
items.detail: For small-to-medium businesses

items.label: Three sections
items.detail: I Property, II Liability, III Common Policy Conditions

items.label: Eligible classes
items.detail: Such as apartments, offices and retail stores

items.label: Not eligible at any size
items.detail: An ordinary bar or tavern

beats.text: A businessowners policy, or BOP, packages property and liability for small-to-medium businesses. It has three sections: property, liability, and common policy conditions.
beats.say: A businessowners policy, or B O P, packages property and liability for small-to-medium businesses. It has three sections: property, liability, and common policy conditions.

beats.text: Eligible classes include apartments, offices and retail stores. But an ordinary bar or tavern isn't an eligible class at any size.
beats.say: Eligible classes include apartments, offices and retail stores. But an ordinary bar or tavern isn't an eligible class at any size.

beats.text: Older lists that exclude all manufacturers and all auto repair are out of date: the 2025 program overview lists light manufacturing and auto service risks as eligible.
beats.say: Older lists that exclude all manufacturers and all auto repair are out of date: the twenty twenty-five program overview lists light manufacturing and auto service risks as eligible.

scenes.q: Under ISO's current businessowners program rules, which business is ineligible for a BOP regardless of its size?
scenes.why: An ordinary bar or tavern is not an eligible BOP class at any size. Offices and retail stores are eligible classes.

beats.text: Quick check. Which of these businesses can't get a BOP, no matter how small it is? Pick an answer.
beats.say: Quick check. Which of these businesses can't get a B O P, no matter how small it is? Pick an answer.

reveal.text: The tavern. An ordinary bar or tavern isn't eligible at any size.
reveal.say: The tavern. An ordinary bar or tavern isn't eligible at any size.

items.label: Open perils
items.detail: Direct physical loss unless excluded or limited

items.label: No coinsurance clause
items.detail: Replacement cost if the limit is at least 80% of full replacement cost

items.label: Building limit grows 8% a year
items.detail: Prorated, unless another percentage is shown

items.label: Business personal property: 25% seasonal bump
items.detail: Only if insured to 100% of average monthly values

beats.text: The property section covers buildings and business personal property on an open perils basis: direct physical loss unless excluded or limited.
beats.say: The property section covers buildings and business personal property on an open perils basis: direct physical loss unless excluded or limited.

beats.text: There's no coinsurance clause. Instead, losses are paid at replacement cost if the limit is at least 80% of full replacement cost.
beats.say: There's no coinsurance clause. Instead, losses are paid at replacement cost if the limit is at least eighty percent of full replacement cost.

beats.text: Two limits grow on their own: the building limit, 8% a year, and business personal property, a 25% seasonal increase if insured to 100% of average monthly values.
beats.say: Two limits grow on their own: the building limit, eight percent a year, and business personal property, a twenty-five percent seasonal increase if insured to one hundred percent of average monthly values.

scenes.title: Under 80%: the BOP's settlement math
scenes.src: ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. I E.5.d(1)(b) (2013 Businessowners form)
given: Repair cost $60,000; ACV of the loss $40,000

items.label: Limit as a share of that

beats.text: Let's work one. A Saginaw shop's building would cost $500,000 to replace. 80% of that is $400,000.
beats.say: Let's work one. A Saginaw shop's building would cost five hundred thousand dollars to replace. Eighty percent of that is four hundred thousand dollars.

beats.text: It's insured for only $300,000, which is 0.75 of what's needed.
beats.say: It's insured for only three hundred thousand dollars, which is zero point seven five of what's needed.

beats.text: The repair costs $60,000, and it's done promptly. 0.75 of that is $45,000.
beats.say: The repair costs sixty thousand dollars, and it's done promptly. Zero point seven five of that is forty-five thousand dollars.

beats.text: The BOP pays the greater of that or actual cash value, here $40,000. So it pays $45,000, ignoring the deductible.
beats.say: The B O P pays the greater of that or actual cash value, here forty thousand dollars. So it pays forty-five thousand dollars, ignoring the deductible.

scenes.title: BOP vs commercial property: numbers that flip

beats.text: Some built-in amounts flip. The fire department service charge is $2,500 in the BOP, but $1,000 in commercial property.
beats.say: Some built-in amounts flip. The fire department service charge is two thousand five hundred dollars in the B O P, but one thousand dollars in commercial property.

beats.text: Outdoor signs flip the other way: $1,000 per attached sign in the BOP, versus $2,500 in commercial property.
beats.say: Outdoor signs flip the other way: one thousand dollars per attached sign in the B O P, versus two thousand five hundred dollars in commercial property.

beats.text: Valuable papers get more in the BOP. And newly acquired buildings get $250,000 for 30 days in both.
beats.say: Valuable papers get more in the B O P. And newly acquired buildings get two hundred fifty thousand dollars for thirty days in both.

scenes.title: Business income is built in
scenes.src: ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. I A.5.f-g, D.3, H.9

items.label: Up to 12 months, no dollar limit
Starts 72 hours after the loss
items.detail: Extra Expense starts immediately

items.label: Ordinary payroll: 60 days
items.detail: Unless more days are shown

items.label: Extended Business Income: 60 days
items.detail: Unless more days are shown

items.label: No deductible
items.detail: Also Extra Expense, Civil Authority, fire department, extinguisher recharge

beats.text: Business Income is built in. It pays actual loss sustained within 12 consecutive months after the loss, with no dollar limit.
beats.say: Business Income is built in. It pays actual loss sustained within twelve consecutive months after the loss, with no dollar limit.

beats.text: It still starts 72 hours after the loss. Extra Expense starts immediately.
beats.say: It still starts seventy-two hours after the loss. Extra Expense starts immediately.

beats.text: Ordinary payroll is covered for 60 days, and Extended Business Income adds up to 60 days after you reopen.
beats.say: Ordinary payroll is covered for sixty days, and Extended Business Income adds up to sixty days after you reopen.

beats.text: No deductible applies to Business Income, Extra Expense, Civil Authority, the fire department service charge or fire extinguisher recharge.
beats.say: No deductible applies to Business Income, Extra Expense, Civil Authority, the fire department service charge or fire extinguisher recharge.

scenes.q: A fire closes a bakery insured under the 2013 ISO Businessowners form for five months. Which statement about its Business Income coverage is correct?
choices: It is capped at the business personal property limit
It pays actual loss sustained within 12 months, with no dollar limit
It begins immediately after the fire, with no waiting period
scenes.why: BOP Business Income pays actual loss sustained within 12 consecutive months after the loss and is not subject to the Section I limits. It begins 72 hours after the loss.

beats.text: Your turn. A fire closes a BOP-insured bakery for five months. Which statement about its Business Income is correct? Pick an answer.
beats.say: Your turn. A fire closes a B O P-insured bakery for five months. Which statement about its Business Income is correct? Pick an answer.

reveal.text: Twelve months, no dollar limit. And it starts after 72 hours, not immediately.
reveal.say: Twelve months, no dollar limit. And it starts after seventy-two hours, not immediately.

items.label: Business Liability
items.detail: Bodily injury, property damage, personal and advertising injury

items.label: Medical Expenses
items.detail: Accidents; incurred and reported within one year

items.label: Each aggregate is 2 times the limit
items.detail: General and products-completed operations

items.label: Professional services excluded
items.detail: Such as legal or accounting services

beats.text: The liability section has two coverages. Business Liability covers bodily injury, property damage, and personal and advertising injury. Medical Expenses pays for accidents, within one year.
beats.say: The liability section has two coverages. Business Liability covers bodily injury, property damage, and personal and advertising injury. Medical Expenses pays for accidents, within one year.

beats.text: There's one Liability and Medical Expenses limit. The general aggregate and the products-completed operations aggregate are each twice that limit.
beats.say: There's one Liability and Medical Expenses limit. The general aggregate and the products-completed operations aggregate are each twice that limit.

beats.text: Professional services, like accounting, are excluded. And who is an insured mirrors the CGL.
beats.say: Professional services, like accounting, are excluded. And who is an insured mirrors the C G L.

scenes.title: Cancellation: the form vs Michigan law
scenes.story: A Bay City shop's building has sat vacant for 70 days, and the insurer wants to cancel the BOP. The 2013 form allows cancellation on 5 days' notice for long vacancy. How much notice is needed in Michigan?

items.label: The 2013 form
items.detail: 5 days if vacant or unoccupied 60 or more consecutive days

items.label: Otherwise, under the form
items.detail: 10 days for nonpayment, 30 days for other reasons

items.label: Michigan law
items.detail: Cancellation notice mailed at least 10 days before, for fire or casualty insurance

scenes.answer: At least 10 days. In Michigan, state law overrides the form's 5-day rule.

beats.text: Now the conditions. A Bay City shop's building has been vacant 70 days, and the insurer wants to cancel. How much notice is needed?
beats.say: Now the conditions. A Bay City shop's building has been vacant seventy days, and the insurer wants to cancel. How much notice is needed?

beats.text: The 2013 form allows 5 days' notice after 60 or more consecutive days of vacancy or unoccupancy. Otherwise, 10 days for nonpayment, 30 for other reasons.
beats.say: The twenty thirteen form allows five days' notice after sixty or more consecutive days of vacancy or unoccupancy. Otherwise, ten days for nonpayment, thirty for other reasons.

beats.text: But in Michigan, state law requires the insurer to mail its cancellation notice at least 10 days before cancellation, for fire and casualty insurance. So: at least 10 days.
beats.say: But in Michigan, state law requires the insurer to mail its cancellation notice at least ten days before cancellation, for fire and casualty insurance. So: at least ten days.

scenes.title: Selected endorsements
scenes.src: ISO IL 04 15 04 98; ISO BP 04 57 01 06; BP 04 30, BP 04 56, BP 04 57 and BP 04 04 as described by FC&S (2020)

items.label: Protective Safeguards
items.detail: P-1 sprinklers, P-2 fire alarm, P-3 security service, P-4 private fire department

items.label: Utility Services: Direct Damage
items.detail: Damage to your property from an off-premises utility interruption

items.label: Utility Services: Time Element
items.detail: Lost income or extra expense from that interruption

items.label: Hired and Non-Owned Auto Liability
items.detail: Hired autos, and autos you don't own, used in your business

beats.text: Four endorsements. Protective Safeguards lists devices you must maintain, like P-1, an automatic sprinkler system, and P-2, an automatic fire alarm.
beats.say: Four endorsements. Protective Safeguards lists devices you must maintain, like P one, an automatic sprinkler system, and P two, an automatic fire alarm.

beats.text: If you knew a safeguard was impaired and didn't tell the insurer, or didn't keep it working, fire losses are excluded.
beats.say: If you knew a safeguard was impaired and didn't tell the insurer, or didn't keep it working, fire losses are excluded.

beats.text: When covered damage to off-premises utility property cuts your service, Direct Damage pays damage to your property, and Time Element pays lost income. Overhead lines count only if scheduled.
beats.say: When covered damage to off-premises utility property cuts your service, Direct Damage pays damage to your property, and Time Element pays lost income. Overhead lines count only if scheduled.

beats.text: And Hired and Non-Owned Auto Liability covers hired autos, and autos you don't own, like an employee's car, used in your business.
beats.say: And Hired and Non-Owned Auto Liability covers hired autos, and autos you don't own, like an employee's car, used in your business.

scenes.q: A fire at an off-premises power substation, which is scheduled as power supply property, cuts a florist's electricity. The florist closes for a week. Which BOP endorsement covers the lost income?
scenes.why: Time Element covers Business Income and Extra Expense from the utility interruption. Direct Damage covers physical damage to covered property.

beats.text: Last one. A fire at a scheduled off-premises power substation cuts a florist's electricity for a week. Which endorsement covers the lost income? Pick an answer.
beats.say: Last one. A fire at a scheduled off-premises power substation cuts a florist's electricity for a week. Which endorsement covers the lost income? Pick an answer.

reveal.text: Time Element. Lost income is time element; Direct Damage covers physical damage to property.
reveal.say: Time Element. Lost income is time element; Direct Damage covers physical damage to property.

scenes.title: Key takeaways
items: An ordinary bar or tavern isn't BOP-eligible at any size
No coinsurance clause; the 80% replacement cost rule instead
Business Income: 12 months, no dollar limit, 72-hour wait
Each liability aggregate is twice the per-occurrence limit
In Michigan, insurer cancellation needs at least 10 days' notice

beats.text: Let's recap. A tavern can't get a BOP. There's no coinsurance, just the 80% rule. Business Income runs 12 months, with no dollar limit.
beats.say: Let's recap. A tavern can't get a B O P. There's no coinsurance, just the eighty percent rule. Business Income runs twelve months, with no dollar limit.

beats.text: Each liability aggregate is twice the limit. And in Michigan, an insurer's cancellation takes at least 10 days' notice.
beats.say: Each liability aggregate is twice the limit. And in Michigan, an insurer's cancellation takes at least ten days' notice.
